sources.title: NVIDIA: Open Agent Safety Platform (Sep 28)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: NVIDIA announced Open Agent Safety Platform Sep 28, 2026 (day-only): open software platform + reference system design for agent testing-to-deployment governance.
claims.context: NVIDIA newsroom Sep 28 + investor release + technical blog (Myers/Watson/Golshan/Arkin) read.

claims.text: Components: OpenShell open-source secure runtime (sandboxed execution, policy enforcement, verifiable tracing), now broadly available; Sentry reference design = out-of-band watchdog on BlueField-4 DPUs (DOCA), ms-scale quarantine, attested telemetry; Vera-optimized, Arm/Intel-extendable.
claims.context: Vendor architecture description; effectiveness is vendor claim.

claims.text: Ecosystem (vendor-stated): 100+ orgs incl. Anthropic Claude Managed Agents, SpaceXAI Cursor/Grok, Scale AI, Salesforce/Slack, SAP Joule; Open Secure AI Alliance (Linux Foundation).
claims.context: Partner quotes are vendor-published; no independent deployment proof.

claims.text: OpenShell + skills via developer resources + GitHub; Sentry is a reference design with no separate price/GA date in the announcement.
claims.context: Availability statement with noted limits; TechRepublic corroborates Sentry reference-design status.

limitations.text: Reference architecture != empirically attack-proof containment; no independent red-team reproduction.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Sentry enforcement depends on BlueField-4 deployment; OpenShell alone excludes it.
